panel.flow.pipeline.processDescription:
Layer 1 — turning all materials (video, presentations, texts, web pages) into text. Idempotent text “snapshots” of each source.

Layer 2 — creating macro-information (summary, topics, key concepts) and ordering the main text WITHOUT compression or loss. Each material gets a structured outline.

Both layers are generated automatically when a material is uploaded. This item reruns the processing of materials that ended with an error. A ready material is processed again with the button in its row.
panel.flow.pipeline.generateDescription:
Two-pass generation of the methodological description of this node’s subtree. Pass 1 (bottom-up) — summarising the child nodes; pass 2 (top-down) — the enclosing context of each node’s position.

Starts a background run; the progress and the result are shown in the status card at the bottom right. Nodes that are already fresh are skipped (memoised by hash).

panel.rolesIntro.screenLead1: The system has analysed the project automatically and proposed a role for each file. Review the list and correct what is needed.
panel.rolesIntro.screenLead2: The system proposes keeping your project’s own files in full. We recommend keeping in full only what is needed to understand the topic of the lesson: then the student’s attention stays on the main thing, and processing the material costs less. The decision is yours.
panel.rolesIntro.title: Why this?
panel.rolesIntro.paragraph1: Only you know for sure which files in this section are key to the student’s learning and which are auxiliary: they create a working environment or simply make the project run. When the system focuses on the key files, it understands your intent better: it is the full files that shape the Mentor’s knowledge and the list of the lesson’s concepts.
panel.rolesIntro.paragraph2: Why not widen the set of full files without need? Besides spreading the system’s attention thin, it is a direct cost — yours or your students’: the more material the system has to work through, the more both the course preparation and the homework reviews cost. But this is not a call to cut everything — keep in full everything that really relates to the topic of this lesson.
panel.rolesIntro.important: Important: the marking concerns only the system’s internal picture of the course. The student downloads the full archive without any cuts.
panel.rolesIntro.strategy1: files that did not pass the security check, and the contents of service folders, were removed by the system during unpacking — they can be neither seen nor brought back;
panel.rolesIntro.strategy2: keep in full what reveals the main ideas of this section;
panel.rolesIntro.strategy3: mark as auxiliary the files you created within the project that are not central to the topic of the lesson: the system will know they are secondary — none of their concepts will become a main concept of the lesson, and the Mentor will keep them only as reference background;
panel.rolesIntro.strategy4: mark as not essential to the topic the automatically generated files, standard libraries and trivial files: the system understands their role and content perfectly well — only a mention in the project tree will remain in the course.
panel.rolesIntro.ackLabel: I have read it, got it

panel.criteria.pass.strict: Work passes when every criterion mandatory for passing ({count}) is met and the score is at least {threshold}.
panel.criteria.pass.score: Work passes when the score is at least {threshold}. No criteria are mandatory for passing.
panel.criteria.pass.modelMustsHint: The weight “essential” was proposed by the system: such criteria count in the score but do not block the pass on their own. To make a criterion decide the pass, make it mandatory for passing.
panel.criteria.criterion.heading: Criterion {id}
panel.criteria.method.modelVerdict: Judged by the system against the text and the sign
panel.criteria.method.mandatoryPoints: Required points: met when the work has every one
panel.criteria.method.softDescent: The system cannot run code yet: for now it judges this criterion against the text and the sign.
panel.criteria.mark.mandatoryHint: Work that does not meet this criterion will not pass, whatever its score.
panel.criteria.mark.scoreOnlyHint: This criterion counts in the score but does not block the pass on its own.
panel.criteria.contradictions.title: What the system noticed in the assignment
panel.criteria.contradictions.lead: Here the assignment contradicts the description of its section. Only you see this: it goes neither into the criteria nor into the score.
panel.criteria.contradictions.fixHint: To remove a contradiction, correct the section description in the “Node description” window or the text of the assignment. A new text is a new version: its list will be composed after the next submission, and your edit will stop applying.
panel.criteria.waiting: Students’ work waiting for the list: {works, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}}.
panel.criteria.status.awaitingFirstSubmi: The list of criteria will be composed after a student first submits work for review; after that you can edit it.
panel.criteria.status.composing: The list of criteria is being composed now. Students’ work waiting for it will be reviewed as soon as it is ready; after that you can edit the list.
panel.criteria.status.taskNotProcessed: The list of criteria has not been composed yet: processing of the assignment text has not finished. If processing is still running, wait for it to finish; if it ended with an error, start it again. The list will then be composed automatically as soon as a student submits work for this assignment, and the work that is waiting will be reviewed at the same time. If no new work is expected soon, contact the system administrator, who will start another attempt.
panel.criteria.status.modelsUnavailable: The list of criteria could not be composed: the service that composes it was temporarily unavailable. Nothing is needed from you: another attempt will be made automatically as soon as a student submits work for this assignment, and the work that is waiting will be reviewed at the same time. If no new work is expected soon or nothing changes, contact the system administrator.
panel.criteria.status.limitReached: The list of criteria could not be composed: the assignment is too large for the limits currently in effect. Contact the system administrator: once the limits are changed, they will start another attempt, and the work that is waiting will be reviewed at the same time. Do not edit the assignment text for this: an edit creates a new version and will not help the work already waiting.
panel.criteria.status.compositionError: The list of criteria could not be composed because of an internal system error. Contact the system administrator: once it is fixed, they will start another attempt, and the work that is waiting will be reviewed at the same time.
panel.criteria.status.notAttempted: No list of criteria has been composed for the current version of the assignment yet, and students’ work is already waiting for it. It will be composed automatically as soon as a student submits work for this assignment, and the work that is waiting will be reviewed at the same time. If no new work is expected soon, contact the system administrator, who will start another attempt.
panel.criteria.status.unknown: There is no list of criteria right now. Refresh the page; if nothing changes, contact the system administrator.
panel.criteria.refusal.notATextTask: This material has no list of criteria: only short assignments, assignments and projects have one. A test is checked by the correct-answer marks in the test editor.
panel.criteria.refusal.taskNotReady: The assignment is still being processed or has been removed from the course. Wait for processing to finish and refresh the page.
panel.criteria.refusal.notFound: Assignment not found: it may have been deleted.
panel.criteria.refusal.noAccess: This access key does not allow editing courses. Sign in with an author’s key.
panel.criteria.refusal.tooManyRequests: Too many requests in a row. Try again in a minute.
panel.criteria.failed.load: Could not load the list of criteria. Check your connection and refresh the page.
panel.criteria.point.removeAllText: Another way of checking has no points: they will be removed from this criterion.
panel.criteria.concepts.hint: Only from the main concepts of the section and the course; up to {max}.
panel.criteria.concepts.empty: The section and the course have no main concepts yet — the “Node description” window sets them.
panel.criteria.mark.switchHint: On — work without this criterion will not pass. Off — the criterion only counts in the score.
panel.criteria.finishFirst: To save the list, fix the marked places.
panel.criteria.saved: The list has been saved: the next work will be reviewed against it.
panel.criteria.leaveText: The changes to the list have not been saved — they will be lost.
panel.criteria.refusal.awaitingFirstSubm: The list was not saved: there is no list for this version of the assignment right now. The page has been refreshed — see what has changed.
panel.criteria.refusal.unknownCriterionI: The list was not saved: it changed while you were editing — for example, in another tab. Your changes stay on the screen; refresh the list and make them again.
panel.criteria.refusal.checkMethodNotAdm: Checking by running the code is only possible in a project. Choose another way of checking in the marked criteria.
panel.criteria.refusal.unknownConcept: The list was not saved: one of the concepts is no longer among the main concepts of the section and the course. The concepts have been refreshed — choose them again in the marked criteria.
panel.criteria.refusal.mustByAuthorWitho: Only a criterion with the weight “essential” can be mandatory for passing. Give it that weight or switch the mark off.
panel.criteria.refusal.invalidField: The list was not saved: fix what is marked in red below.
panel.criteria.failed.save: Could not save the list. Check your connection and try again — your changes stay on the screen.
panel.criteria.problem.pointEmpty: Enter the point or remove it.
panel.criteria.problem.noPoints: Add at least one required point or choose another way of checking.
panel.criteria.problem.noCriteria: The list must have at least one criterion. To return to the system’s list, use “Return to the system’s list”.
panel.criteria.problem.tooManyCriteria: The list can have no more than {max} criteria.
